p: Here's the thing about St Mary Axe: by day it's one of the most serious-looking streets in Britain. The Gherkin rises right overhead, the inside-out Lloyd's building sits a few steps away, and everyone seems to be walking at double speed with a coffee in hand. That's exactly why a bowling lane round here feels like such a cheeky little escape. One minute you're in the engine room of the City, the next you're arguing about whether your foot went over the line.

Getting here is dead easy. Liverpool Street, Aldgate and Bank are all within a comfortable walk, so it works whether your crew are coming from Essex, the East End or the other side of the river. If a few of you are heading straight from the office, it's worth agreeing a meeting point outside, as the streets round the towers all start to look the same after dark.

A few tips to get the most from it. Mix up the teams so the confident bowlers aren't all on one lane, because a close score makes for a much louder night. Pop a pair of socks in your bag, as bowling venues usually hand out shoes. And if you're organising for a big group, sort the numbers early and nominate one person to wrangle the booking, or it'll turn into forty emails and no lane.
Fancy a view first? The Sky Garden at the top of the Walkie-Talkie on Fenchurch Street is close by and gives you a proper eyeful of the City before you get stuck into the frames.
